Bram has stood his sword by the door.
Its point faces outward.
값을 깎지 않는 집이라 또 왔소.\n빚진 기분 없이 자는 곳은\n드물거든:
Back again. You don't haggle here.
Few places let a man sleep
owing nothing.
지난번 할아버지 얘기 말이오.\n털어놓고 나니… 이상하게\n잠이 잘 왔소:
About my grandfather, last time.
Once I'd said it… strangely,
I slept well.
그런데 마을에선 날 두고\n'마녀 집 문지기'라 부르더군.\n…비웃는 거:
But in the village they call me
'the witch's doorkeeper.'
…They mean it as a jeer.
인간이 문지기라니, 숲이 웃겠군요.\n…하지만 문을 지키는 손은\n횃불을:
A human doorkeeper? The woods laugh.
…Yet a hand that guards a door
beats one that carries a torch.
…Sharp ears, my fairy lord.
I'll take that as praise.
Worse than the jeering: his face says
he rather likes the name.
하! 품삯 받으면 진짜 문지기 되지.\n공짜라야 내 마음대로\n서 있다:
Ha! Take wages and I'm a real one.
Unpaid, I can stand where I like
and leave when I like.
'문지기면 어떻소, 안에 수프가 있는데.'\n…그 뒤로 아무도 안 웃더군:
'Doorkeeper? There's soup inside.'
…None laughed after that.
A few asked the way.
The way to this house.
Tonight the point faces out again.
…There's no call to face inward.
Bram sets an old lantern on the table.
Its soot is thick.
할아버지 유품이오.\n횃불을 내려놓은 뒤로\n평생 이 등불만 들고 다녔다:
My grandfather's. After he laid down
his torch, they say he carried
only this lantern all his life.
'Light leads to the witch's house.'
…I told you that first, of all folk.
Now I think I see what he meant.
죽기 전에 이상한 말을 했소.\n'불빛을 따라가면 마녀 집이 나온다.'\:
He said an odd thing before he died.
'Light leads to the witch's house.'
…Now I think I see what he meant.
I'll leave this lamp in your window,
so lost folk can follow it.
A witch hunter's lantern,
lighting the road from her window.
…Should I take it?
In the window. You bring the oil.
…Done. I'll stop by every third day.
On account of the oil.
A man who leaves no debts
has made his first excuse.
…Aye. It's my burden to carry.
Not your window's.
그럼 길에서 이 불빛을 보는 놈은\n이 집 쪽으로 데려오겠소.\n그건 되:
Then any soul I see on the road
by this light, I'll bring this way.
That'll do?
Grandfather bore fire to hunt witches.
I bore fire to find a witch's house.
Mira sets down her herb basket.
On top lies frost-touched primrose.
You said it was just a weed, yes?
Yet this weed closed a wound
so quickly. Look at this.
그 책이요, 다시 봤어요.\n찢긴 첫 장 뒷면에\n눈송이 같은 표식이 남:
I looked at that book again.
On the back of the torn first page
there was a mark like a snowflake.
할머니는 그 책을 '빌린 책'이라고만\n했어요. 누구한테서인지는\n끝까지:
Grandmother only called it
'a borrowed book.' From whom,
she never told me, to the end.
Child, a borrowed book goes back.
Even after a hundred years.
…백 년이요? 할머니, 그 책 아세요?: …A hundred years? You know it, Gran?
모른다. 드워프는 책보다\n빌려 간 놈 얼굴을 기억하지.\n…밥이나 먹어:
I don't. Dwarves remember the face
of the borrower, not the book.
…Eat your supper.
Snowflake: the North Witch's mark.
…My grandmother's grandmother's.
그 책, 나한테 보여 줄 수 있어?: Could you show me that book?
…가져오면 돌려 달라고 하실 거죠?: …You'll want it back if I bring it?
아, 아니에요. 원래 주인이면\n돌려드리는 게 맞죠.\n다음에 꼭 가져올:
Oh, no, that's fair. If it's yours,
it ought to go back to you.
I'll bring it next time, truly.
Keep it borrowed, as she said.
빌린 책으로요?\n…그럼 제가 계속 빌리고 있는 거네요.\n갚을 게 늘었:
Borrowed, then?
…So I'm still borrowing it.
More debt to repay. I'll pay in herbs.
Tonight I'll glue the first page back.
With bread paste. Your bread, Witch.
I brought it. As I promised.
…My hands are shaking. Why?
The witch's hand stops on a page.
Every margin holds a familiar hand.
책은 안 가져왔어요.\n대신 겨울 약초 장만 베껴 왔어요.\n제 글씨라:
I didn't bring the book.
But I copied the winter herb pages.
In my own hand, so it's a mess.
책에 이런 구절이 있어요.\n'겨울에 피는 풀은\n누군가 아직 이 집에:
There's a line in the book:
'A herb that blooms in winter
means someone still lives here.'
So it blooms in winter.
Because I live here.
…'누군가 산다는 뜻'이면\n제 집에도 사람은 사니까요.\n해 볼게요!:
…If it means 'someone lives here,'
well, someone lives at mine too.
I'll try!
Tell no one else that line.
…네. 약초꾼은 입이 무거워요.\n독초가 어디 나는지도\n아무한테나 안:
…Yes. Herb-folk keep quiet.
We don't tell just anyone
where the poison herbs grow.
I see why Grandmother cherished it.
…She wasn't the borrower.
She was the keeper, I think.
Brought you a deer. As promised.
…No surcharge for it, mind.
Outside the door a deer lies
under a dusting of snow. A big one.
오늘은 토끼 두 마리요.\n사슴은 눈치가 빨라서.\n…수프에 넣어 주시오:
Two hares today.
Deer are quick to scent you.
…Put them in the soup.
호위하던 상단이 흩어졌소.\n대장이 돈 궤를 들고 사라졌지.\n…석 달:
The caravan I guarded scattered.
The captain fled with the strongbox.
…Three months' wages.
혹시 '회색 말' 상단이에요?\n장터에 소문 났어요.\n대장이 남쪽 항구:
Was it the 'Grey Horse' caravan?
The market's full of it.
They say he went to the south port.
…South, is it. Thanks, trader.
The market hears it first.
A stony face, yet
his grip on the spoon is tight.
…Chasing him costs three more months.
For that money. The sums don't add.
…품삯은 못 주는 집이잖소.\n수프로 받으라는 거요?:
…You can't pay wages here.
You'd have me paid in soup?
…Not bad.
If there's meat in it.
Just one bowl tonight.
…No, two.
Anger makes me hungry.
Found new work. Guarding a waystation
on the north border. Half a day off.
겨울 내내 여기서 사냥한 덕에\n활 솜씨가 늘었소.\n새 대장이 그걸 보:
All winter hunting here
sharpened my bow arm.
The new captain saw and took me.
결국 안 쫓아갔소.\n대신 새 대장 얼굴을 오래 봤지.\n이번 대장은 돈:
I never went after him.
I took a long look at the new captain.
This one doesn't smell of coin.
그래서 묻는 거요.\n역참 사람들한테 이 집 수프를\n…소문내도 되겠소?:
So I'm asking.
May I tell the waystation folk
…about the soup here?
Ha. That goblin peddler's sales cry?
That's reached the border already.
…Understood. Of the four waystations,
this is the best. That much
I'll keep to myself.
Three waystations, did I say?
…Four now. Counting this one.
The old mountain road.
Folk come by it these days.
Not just me.
길이 아직 쓸 만하다고 했지.\n…그 말을 술집에서 했더니\n이렇게 됐소:
I said the road was still good.
…Said it in a tavern, and
now look. That's on me.
문양을 안 지웠소.\n그랬더니 문양을 따라온 사람들이\n생겼소. 길잡이도:
I left the marks alone.
And folk began to follow them.
No guide needed.
피난민이오. 남쪽 마을이\n'뭔가'에 쫓겨 비었다더군.\n…다들 이 집을:
Refugees. A southern village
fled from 'something,' they say.
…All of them seek this house.
길잡이 밥줄 끊겼네요, 토르빈 씨.\n우리 여우들은 그 길 안 써요.\n:
There goes your living, Master Torbin.
We foxes don't use that road.
The marks look too much like eyes.
South. The Southern Sister's land.
…Is the seal stone there still safe?
…There won't be rooms enough.
Then I'll sleep in the stable.
I always liked rooms far from windows.
A stable has none.
Mark the head of the road.
A mark. One more by the old ones?
…Shall I carve 'No Rooms'?
A jest.
I'll carve one more lantern.
길잡이가 길을 안 숨기니\n먹고살 게 줄겠군.\n…이상하게 서운하지 않소:
A guide who won't hide his road
will have less to live on.
…Strange, I don't mind.
I raised a new waymark.
Beside the old one.
Carved one more lantern mark, too.
…Crooked, as it's my handiwork.
물어볼 게 있소.\n옛 이정표를 세운 건 누구요?\n…마녀였소? 아니면:
A question for you.
Who raised the old waymark?
…A witch? Or someone else?
돌에 새긴 손이 둘이었다고\n오스윈이 말했었다.\n마녀의 손과… 다른 손:
Two hands carved the stone,
Oswin had said.
A witch's hand… and another.
A friend. So before the witch hunt
witches had friends too.
…Plain enough, yet
I'd never thought of it.
…그렇군. 길잡이는\n길 끝만 알면 되오.\n누가 닦았는지는 돌이 알겠지:
…I see. A guide need only know
where the road ends.
Who cleared it, the stones know.
I carved no name on my waymark.
…That I learned from them.
'숲의 마녀' 앞 편지,\n하나를 잃어버렸어요!\n배달부 인생 최대 사고:
A letter for 'the Witch of the Wood'…
I lost one!
Worst blunder of my courier life!
가져오라고 하셔서 챙겼는데\n…가방 구멍으로 하나가.\n나머지 아홉 통은:
You said to bring them, so I did,
…but one slipped through a hole.
The other nine are right here!
안 읽었어요! 정말로!\n…근데 잃어버린 건 봉투가 찢어져서\n조금 보였:
I didn't read them! Truly!
…But the lost one's seal was torn,
so I saw a little. Just a little.
'숲의 마녀님, 그 겨울에\n제 아이를 살려 주셔서…'\n거기까지요! 진:
'Witch of the Wood, that winter
you saved my child…'
That's all! Truly, that's all!
편지 한 통이면 숲길 어딘가에서\n누가 주워 읽겠지.\n…기록은 원래 그:
A lost letter on a forest path:
someone will pick it up and read.
…That is how records ever spread.
That winter.
I remember which winter.
괜찮다고요? 배달부한테\n그건 제일 무서운 말인데…:
All right? For a courier, that's
the most frightening thing…
…But thank you.
I nearly cried. No, I cried a bit.
Let's go look for it together.
진짜요? 마녀님이 숲길에?: Truly? You, Witch, on the forest path?
…그럼 편지가 무서워서\n알아서 튀어나오겠네요!:
…Then the letter will be so scared
it'll jump out on its own!
Next time I'll mend my bag first.
…Now where did I put the thread.
이번엔 반대예요!: This time it's the other way!
마녀님이 답장을 쓰시면\n제가 배달할게요.\n이번엔 안 잃어버려요!:
If you write replies, Witch,
I'll deliver them.
I won't lose them this time!
그날 같이 찾은 편지,\n개울가 바위 밑에 있었잖아요.\n…거기 주소가:
The letter we found that day
was under a stone by the stream.
…It had the address on it.
The senders all live in the village.
The ten who wrote 'thank you.'
If I answer, ten households
will know for sure a witch lives here.
…Good. Short letters
last the longest.
A courier knows.
…그럼 제가 말로 전할게요.\n'편지 잘 받았대요.'\n그 정도는 배달부:
…Then I'll tell them by mouth.
'She got your letters.'
That much is a courier's call.
My bag is light today.
…Somehow that makes it heavier.
I copied more of the marks.
The second hand was left-handed.
The strokes lean the other way.
모르는 척하라고 했지.\n…그래서 책엔 안 적고\n머릿속에만 적었소. 더:
You said to feign ignorance.
…So I wrote it not in my book
but in my head. It weighs more.
말한 대로 기록은 난로 곁에 두었소.\n…주인 몰래 반 장은 탔소.\n불:
My notes stay by the hearth, as told.
…Half a page burned behind your back.
The fire was too pleasant.
왼손잡이 석공은 드물지.\n그런데 이 집 들보 이음새도\n왼쪽으로 기울었:
Left-handed masons are rare.
Yet the beam joints in this house
lean to the left as well.
맞소. 들보 짠 손은 왼손이오.\n쐐기 없이.\n…드워프도 못 하는 솜씨:
Aye. A left hand joined these beams.
Without a single wedge.
…Beyond even a dwarf's craft.
할머니의 할머니는 오른손잡이였다.\n그럼 이 집을 지은 건…:
My grandmother's gran: right-handed.
Then this house was built by…
…Together. A witch and a warlock
raising one roof between them.
Then what, in truth,
did the witch hunt sever?
알겠소. 하지만 나는 기록가요.\n멈추라면 멈추지만\n잊으라는 말은 못:
Very well. But I am a chronicler.
Tell me to stop and I'll stop,
but I cannot be told to forget.
I'll spare the ink tonight.
…There's more I cannot write.
Oswin holds out a leather ledger.
It is blank from first page to last.
이 집에 대한 기록이오.\n…아무것도 안 적었소.\n적으면 누군가 읽을:
My record of this house.
…I wrote nothing.
What's written, someone will read.
마녀와 그 '다른 손'이\n함께 지은 집이라는 것.\n그건 책보다 돌에:
That the witch and that 'other hand'
built this house together…
that I leave to stone, not books.
A blank ledger.
The longest record he could write.
That anyone may read.
Even a witch hunter.
Leave it blank. I'll keep it.
주인이 빈 장부를 맡는다.\n…기록가로서 이보다 나은\n결말은 못 썼을:
The innkeeper keeps the blank ledger.
…As a chronicler, I could not
have written a better ending.
다음 유적은 동쪽이오.\n거기에도 두 손이 있다면\n또 오겠소. 잉크를:
The next ruin lies east.
If two hands are there as well,
I'll return, with fresh ink.
The rumor about your wool, Witch?
Someone's coming to 'check' it.
셋으로 나누자고 했잖아요.\n그 말 하고 다녔더니\n값이 진짜 두 배가:
You said to split it three ways.
I went about saying so,
and the price truly doubled!
그냥 양털이라고 하셨죠.\n그 말 했더니 아무도 안 믿어요.\n'마녀가:
You said it's just wool.
I told them, and nobody believes it.
'The witch hides it,' they say.
오는 사람은 남쪽 모직 조합\n감독관이에요.\n…돈 냄새 맡는 코가 길어:
It's the inspector from
the southern wool guild.
…Long nose for the smell of coin.
그 감독관 말이오?\n지난달 내 좌판에서 깎다가\n동전 하나 떨어뜨리고:
That inspector?
Haggled at my stall last month
and dropped a coin as he left.
그 동전 돌려줬어요, 브로크 씨?: Did you give it back, Master Brock?
…What drops on my stall stays there.
그리고… 그 검은 양이요.\n그건 소문 내지 마세요.\n검은 양털은 값을:
And… that black sheep.
Don't let word of it out.
Black wool can't even be priced.
양털이 비에 안 젖는 건 사실이다.\n양이 아니라, 울타리에 건\n서리:
It's true the wool shrugs off rain.
Not thanks to the sheep, but the
frost ward hung on the fence.
Show the inspector some wet wool.
하! 물통에 담갔다 꺼낸 걸로요?: Ha! Wool dunked in a water trough?
…Fine, I'll do the acting.
Traders are half players anyway.
Tell him to come and see.
여기로요? 감독관이 마녀 집에?: Here? An inspector, at a witch's?
…If he comes, charge him double.
I'll waive my cut. Just this once.
Give the sheep good grass tonight.
…They must play innocent, after all.
감독관 다녀갔어요.\n젖은 양털 보고 코웃음 치더니\n'소문은 소문'이래:
The inspector came and went.
He sniffed at the wet wool:
'A rumor's a rumor.' Success!
감독관이 진짜 왔다 갔어요.\n하룻밤 묵고 아무 말 없이\n양털 한 묶음:
The inspector really did come.
Stayed a night, said not a word,
and paid dear for a bundle of wool.
But here's the odd part.
As he left, he said to me…
'The innkeeper there sounds like the one
my grandmother used to speak of.'
The inspector's grandmother.
Someone else remembers this house.
…I'll find out. But my fee
is paid in wool. Not the wet kind.
…But Witch, you just smiled.
A little. I saw it.
다음엔 모직 조합 도장 찍힌\n주문서 들고 올게요.\n'안 젖는 양털,:
Next time I'll bring an order
sealed by the wool guild:
'Rainproof wool, three bundles.'
Saw the lamp in your window.
…Time I filled the oil.
등불 들고 왔소.\n길에서 둘을 이리 보냈지.\n…방 있소?:
Brought the lantern.
Sent two folk this way on the road.
…Any rooms?
값 안 깎는 집이라 또 왔소.\n…수프 값은 똑같지?:
Back again. You don't haggle here.
…Soup's the same price?
One bloomed outside my house too!
In winter! I wanted to show you.
You remember the book, don't you?
I've not come empty-handed today.
I keep thinking of that torn page.
…I'll impose on you again tonight.
Winter hunting season again.
Followed the smell of soup.
I kept my word about the deer.
Just soup today. I'll pay.
Folk on the road again today.
…All headed this way.
Came by the old mountain road.
…The marks still point here.
All the replies delivered!
All ten houses wept. Me too.
I mended my bag this time!
…One side of it.
Is the blank ledger well?
…It comes to mind now and then.
Came to see the beams first.
…Greetings can wait.
감독관 다녀간 뒤로\n장터에서 제 값이 올랐어요!\n오늘은 제가 차 살게:
Since the inspector's visit
my prices at market have risen!
Tea's on me today.
Brought the shares, split three ways.
…The sheep's share is in grass.
